admission-controller.md.title: Kubernetes Admission Controller Overview
admission-controller.md.summary: This document describes Admission Controllers, which intercept requests to the Kubernetes API server before object persistence. They can validate or mutate incoming requests, allowing for request rejection or modification.

admission-policies.md.title: Validating and Mutating Admission Policies
admission-policies.md.summary: This document explains declarative admission policies, which use Common Expression Language (CEL) to validate or mutate resources directly within the API server. It covers both ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and MutatingAdmissionPolicy types.

admission-webhooks-good-practices.md.title: Admission Webhook Good Practices
admission-webhooks-good-practices.md.summary: This document outlines best practices for designing and implementing admission webhooks in Kubernetes. It covers topics like performance, idempotence, avoiding loops, and ensuring robust deployment for cluster operators.

affinity.md.title: Kubernetes Pod Affinity Rules
affinity.md.summary: This document explains Kubernetes affinity, which provides hints to the scheduler regarding pod placement. It details the two types of affinity: node affinity and pod-to-pod affinity.

aggregation-layer.md.title: Kubernetes Aggregation Layer
aggregation-layer.md.summary: This document explains the Aggregation Layer, which allows users to install additional Kubernetes-style APIs within their cluster. It details how to use APIService objects to claim specific URL paths in the Kubernetes API.

annotation.md.title: Annotation Metadata
annotation.md.summary: This document defines an annotation as a key-value pair used to attach arbitrary, non-identifying metadata to objects. It explains that this metadata can be of various sizes and structures, and can be retrieved by client tools.

api-group.md.title: Kubernetes API Group Overview
api-group.md.summary: This document explains the concept of an API Group within Kubernetes. It describes how API groups organize related paths in the Kubernetes API and how they are used for extending the API.

api-resource.md.title: Kubernetes API Resource Definition
api-resource.md.summary: This document defines an API resource within the Kubernetes type system. It explains that a resource corresponds to an endpoint on the Kubernetes API server, defining schemas for objects or operations.

api-server-bypass-risks.md.title: Kubernetes API Server Bypass Risks
api-server-bypass-risks.md.summary: This document details various methods by which security controls within the Kubernetes API server can be bypassed. It focuses on risks associated with Static Pods, the kubelet API, and the etcd API.

app-container.md.title: Application Containers in Pods
app-container.md.summary: This document defines application containers, which are the primary containers in a pod that start after initialization is complete. It explains the role of app containers versus init containers within a pod.

application-architect.md.title: Application Architect Role and Responsibilities
application-architect.md.summary: This document defines the role of an Application Architect. It explains that the architect is responsible for the high-level design, ensuring the application is scalable and maintainable when interacting with surrounding components.

application-security-checklist.md.title: Application Security Checklist for Kubernetes
application-security-checklist.md.summary: This checklist provides guidelines for securing applications deployed in Kubernetes from a developer's perspective. It covers various security aspects from application design to container and pod configurations.

approver.md.title: Kubernetes Code Approver Role
approver.md.summary: This document defines the role of an Approver for Kubernetes code contributions. Approval focuses on holistic acceptance, including compatibility, API adherence, and system interactions, distinguishing it from code quality review.

architecture.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Architecture Overview
architecture.md.summary: This document describes the architecture of a Kubernetes cluster, detailing the roles of the control plane and worker nodes. It explains the function of core components necessary for a complete and operational cluster.

authentication-mechanisms.md.title: Hardening Guide: Kubernetes Authentication Mechanisms
authentication-mechanisms.md.summary: This guide details various authentication mechanisms available in Kubernetes, such as X.509 certificates and various token types. It advises on selecting appropriate methods for production environments, recommending external sources like OIDC for multi-user access.

authorization.md.title: Kubernetes API Server Authorization
authorization.md.summary: This document details how Kubernetes authorizes API requests within the API server. It explains the process of determining whether a request is allowed or denied based on various request attributes and configured authorization modules.

autoscaling.md.title: Kubernetes Workload Autoscaling Strategies
autoscaling.md.summary: This document explains how to scale workloads in Kubernetes, covering both manual and automatic scaling methods. It details horizontal and vertical scaling, including the use of HPA and VPA.

cadvisor.md.title: cAdvisor Overview
cadvisor.md.summary: cAdvisor is a daemon that collects, aggregates, and exports resource usage and performance data for running containers. It provides detailed metrics including resource isolation parameters, historical usage, and network statistics.

cdi.md.title: Container Device Interface (CDI) Specification
cdi.md.summary: This document describes the Container Device Interface (CDI), a specification for configuring devices within containers. It explains how Kubernetes uses CDI with device plugins and Dynamic Resource Allocation to provide workloads with necessary device setups.

cel.md.title: Common Expression Language (CEL)
cel.md.summary: This document describes Common Expression Language (CEL), a fast, portable, and safe general-purpose expression language. It explains how CEL can be used within Kubernetes for querying and fine-grained filtering.

certificate.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Access Certificates
certificate.md.summary: This document describes the role of certificates in a Kubernetes cluster. Certificates are cryptographically secure files used to validate client access to the Kubernetes API securely.

cgroup.md.title: Linux cgroup Overview
cgroup.md.summary: This document introduces cgroup, a Linux kernel feature. It explains how cgroup allows for resource isolation, accounting, and limiting of resource usage for groups of processes.

cidr.md.title: CIDR Notation for IP Addressing
cidr.md.summary: This document explains CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing), a notation used to describe blocks of IP addresses. It details how CIDR is utilized in Kubernetes to assign unique IP ranges to Nodes and Pods for both IPv4 and IPv6.

cla.md.title: Contributor License Agreement (CLA)
cla.md.summary: This document explains the Contributor License Agreement (CLA). It outlines the terms under which contributors grant a license to an open-source project for their submitted contributions.

cloud-controller-manager.md.title: Cloud Controller Manager Overview
cloud-controller-manager.md.summary: This document describes the Cloud Controller Manager, a Kubernetes control plane component. It explains how it embeds cloud-specific control logic to link the cluster with a cloud provider's API.

cloud-native-security.md.title: Cloud Native Security with Kubernetes
cloud-native-security.md.summary: This document provides an overview of cloud native information security practices, specifically within the context of Kubernetes. It details security controls across various lifecycle phases, including development, distribution, deployment, and runtime.

cloud-provider.md.title: Cloud Provider Overview
cloud-provider.md.summary: This document defines cloud providers, which offer cloud computing platforms and services. It explains different service models, including Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) and Platform as a Service (PaaS) with managed Kubernetes.

cluster-administration.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Administration Overview
cluster-administration.md.summary: This document provides an overview for creating and administering Kubernetes clusters. It covers planning, managing, and securing clusters, including details on networking, access control, and node management.

cluster-operations.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Operations Management
cluster-operations.md.summary: This document outlines the scope of managing a Kubernetes cluster. It covers day-to-day operational tasks, including scaling, upgrades, security implementation, and managing cluster-wide observability.

cluster-operator.md.title: Cluster Operator Role and Responsibilities
cluster-operator.md.summary: This document defines the role of a Cluster Operator. Their primary responsibility is maintaining the operational health of clusters through configuration, control, monitoring, and performing necessary maintenance or upgrades.

cluster.md.title: Cluster Overview
cluster.md.summary: This document defines a cluster as a set of worker machines (nodes) that run containerized applications. It explains the roles of worker nodes, Pods, and the control plane in managing the cluster.

cncf.md.title: Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF)
cncf.md.summary: This document introduces the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), which fosters ecosystems for orchestrating containers in microservices architectures. It explains the CNCF's mission to make cloud native computing ubiquitous.

cni.md.title: Container Network Interface (CNI) Specification
cni.md.summary: This document describes Container Network Interface (CNI) plugins, which are network plugins adhering to the appc/CNI specification. It provides context for understanding how container networking is managed.

components.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Components Overview
components.md.summary: This document provides a high-level overview of the essential components that constitute a Kubernetes cluster. It details the roles of core components, including those in the control plane and on worker nodes.

condition.md.title: Kubernetes Resource Conditions
condition.md.summary: This document explains the concept of a 'Condition' field within a Kubernetes resource's status. It details how conditions standardize status reporting using types, statuses (True/False/Unknown), and optional details like reason and message.

configuration.md.title: Kubernetes Configuration Methods
configuration.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes allows configuration to be separated from application code. It details various methods, including using ConfigMaps and Secrets, and leveraging sidecar or init containers for configuration injection.

container-env-variables.md.title: Container Environment Variables
container-env-variables.md.summary: This document explains container environment variables, which are name=value pairs passed into running containers. They provide necessary information for applications, including file system details and cluster resource endpoints.

container-runtime.md.title: Container Runtime in Kubernetes
container-runtime.md.summary: This document describes the role of the Container Runtime, which is essential for Kubernetes to execute containers. It explains that the runtime manages the lifecycle and execution of containers within the Kubernetes environment.

container.md.title: Container Definition and Concept
container.md.summary: This document defines a container as a lightweight, portable executable image containing software and its dependencies. It explains how containers decouple applications from host infrastructure for easier deployment and scaling.

containerd.md.title: containerd Overview
containerd.md.summary: containerd is a container runtime daemon for Linux and Windows. It manages core container functions, including image fetching, storage, execution, and networking.

containers.md.title: Containers and Container Images Overview
containers.md.summary: This document explains containers, which decouple applications from host infrastructure, ensuring repeatable deployments. It details container images as ready-to-run packages and discusses the role of container runtimes in execution.

contributor.md.title: Kubernetes Contributor Guide
contributor.md.summary: This document defines what a contributor is within the Kubernetes project or community. It outlines various ways individuals can contribute, such as submitting pull requests, reporting issues, or participating in SIGs.

control-plane.md.title: Container Orchestration Control Plane Components
control-plane.md.summary: This document describes the Control Plane, the orchestration layer responsible for managing the lifecycle of containers via an API. It details the core components that make up this layer.

cpu-constraint-namespace.md.title: Configuring CPU Constraints with LimitRange in Kubernetes
cpu-constraint-namespace.md.summary: This document explains how to enforce minimum and maximum CPU resource constraints for Pods within a Kubernetes namespace. It details the use of the LimitRange object to automatically manage resource requests and limits for containers.

cpu-default-namespace.md.title: Configuring Default CPU Requests and Limits in a Kubernetes Namespace
cpu-default-namespace.md.summary: This document explains how to configure default CPU requests and limits for a Kubernetes namespace using a LimitRange. It details how the control plane applies these defaults when Pods do not specify resource requests or limits.

cri-o.md.title: CRI-O Overview
cri-o.md.summary: CRI-O is a tool that implements the Kubernetes Container Runtime Interface (CRI). It enables Kubernetes to use OCI-compliant container runtimes and fetch images from remote registries.

cron-jobs.md.title: CronJob Definition and Usage
cron-jobs.md.summary: This document explains the CronJob resource, which schedules Jobs to run periodically based on a specified Cron syntax. It details scheduling, limitations, and how to define and modify CronJobs.

csi.md.title: Container Storage Interface (CSI)
csi.md.summary: This document explains the Container Storage Interface (CSI), which provides a standard way to expose storage systems to containers in Kubernetes. It allows vendors to create custom storage plugins without modifying the core Kubernetes repository.

customresourcedefinition.md.title: CustomResourceDefinition (CRD)
customresourcedefinition.md.summary: This document explains CustomResourceDefinitions (CRDs), which are API objects used to extend the Kubernetes API server. They allow users to add custom API resources without needing to build a complete custom server.

daemonset.md.title: DaemonSet Overview and Specification
daemonset.md.summary: This document explains what a DaemonSet is, ensuring a copy of a Pod runs on every (or selected) Node in a cluster. It details how to write the DaemonSet specification, including required fields like the Pod Template and Pod Selector.

debug-application.md.title: Troubleshooting Containerized Applications
debug-application.md.summary: This document provides resources for resolving issues within containerized applications. It covers common problems with Kubernetes resources, interpreting container termination messages, and debugging running containers.

debug-cluster.md.title: Troubleshooting Kubernetes Clusters
debug-cluster.md.summary: This document provides guidance on troubleshooting issues within a cluster environment, assuming the application itself is not the root cause. It covers checking node status, examining logs, and understanding various cluster failure modes.

debug.md.title: Monitoring, Logging, and Debugging Guide
debug.md.summary: This guide provides resources for troubleshooting issues within a system. It directs users to specific documentation for debugging applications, clusters, and managing logging and monitoring in Kubernetes.

deployment.md.title: Kubernetes Deployments Overview
deployment.md.summary: This document explains Kubernetes Deployments, which provide declarative updates for Pods and ReplicaSets. It details various operations such as creating, updating, scaling, rolling back, and managing the lifecycle of deployments.

device-plugin.md.title: Device Plugin Overview
device-plugin.md.summary: This document explains Device Plugins, which run on worker Nodes to give Pods access to infrastructure resources like local hardware. They advertise these resources to the kubelet so workloads can utilize specific hardware features.

device-plugins.md.title: Kubernetes Device Plugins Overview
device-plugins.md.summary: This document explains the Kubernetes device plugin framework, allowing vendors to advertise specialized hardware resources like GPUs or FPGAs to the kubelet. It details the registration process, resource advertising, and how Pods request these extended resources.

device.md.title: Device Definition and Usage
device.md.summary: This document defines a 'Device' as infrastructure resources attached to nodes, which can be commercial products like GPUs or custom hardware. It explains that these devices typically require device drivers for Kubernetes Pods to access them.

deviceclass.md.title: DeviceClass for Dynamic Resource Allocation
deviceclass.md.summary: DeviceClass categorizes devices within the cluster for use with Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA). It allows administrators to define sets of devices that can be claimed by workloads using ResourceClaims.

disruption.md.title: Understanding Pod Disruptions
disruption.md.summary: This document defines disruptions as events causing Pods to go out of service. It distinguishes between voluntary disruptions (like manual Pod destruction) and involuntary disruptions (like Node failures).

dns-pod-service.md.title: Kubernetes DNS for Services and Pods
dns-pod-service.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes automatically creates DNS records for Services and Pods, allowing components to communicate using names instead of IP addresses. It details concepts like namespaces, record types (A/AAAA, SRV), and DNS resolution behavior.

docker.md.title: Docker Engine Overview
docker.md.summary: This document introduces Docker, a technology that provides operating-system-level virtualization through containers. It explains how Docker uses Linux kernel features like cgroups and namespaces to run isolated containers efficiently.

dockershim.md.title: Dockershim Component Overview
dockershim.md.summary: This document describes dockershim, a component used in Kubernetes versions 1.23 and earlier. It explains how dockershim enabled the kubelet to communicate with the Docker Engine.

downstream.md.title: Downstream (Disambiguation)
downstream.md.summary: This document clarifies the term 'downstream' in technical contexts. It explains how the term is used to refer to dependent code in the Kubernetes ecosystem or to forked repositories in Git.

downward-api.md.title: Downward API for Injecting Pod/Container Information
downward-api.md.summary: This document explains the Downward API, which allows containers to access information about themselves or the cluster without direct Kubernetes API interaction. It details available fields accessible via `fieldRef` and `resourceFieldRef`.

drain.md.title: kubectl drain command for Node maintenance
drain.md.summary: This document explains the process of safely evicting Pods from a Node using the `kubectl drain` command. It details how this command marks a Node as unavailable for maintenance and handles eviction retries.

dual-stack.md.title: IPv4/IPv6 Dual-Stack Networking in Kubernetes
dual-stack.md.summary: This document explains how IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack networking enables Pods and Services to have both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. It details prerequisites, configuration methods, and service-specific dual-stack options.

duration.md.title: Kubernetes Duration Format
duration.md.summary: This document explains the string format used to represent time durations within Kubernetes APIs. Durations are expressed as a sum of non-negative integers combined with specific time unit suffixes.

dynamic-volume-provisioning.md.title: Dynamic Volume Provisioning Overview
dynamic-volume-provisioning.md.summary: This document explains Dynamic Volume Provisioning, a feature that allows users to automatically request and create storage Volumes. It details how this process relies on an API object, StorageClass, to interact with a Volume Plugin.

endpoint-slice.md.title: EndpointSlice Overview
endpoint-slice.md.summary: This document explains EndpointSlices, which track the IP addresses of backend endpoints associated with a Service. It details how Kubernetes uses these slices to represent the backing endpoints, typically Pods.

endpoint-slices.md.title: EndpointSlice Resource Documentation
endpoint-slices.md.summary: This document explains the EndpointSlice API in Kubernetes, which groups network endpoints for a Service. It details how EndpointSlices are created, their structure, and the conditions used to manage endpoint status.

endpoint.md.title: Deprecated Endpoints API
endpoint.md.summary: This document describes the deprecated Endpoints API, which represented the set of all endpoints for a Service. Kubernetes now uses EndpointSlices instead due to scalability concerns.

ephemeral-container.md.title: Ephemeral Container Usage
ephemeral-container.md.summary: This document describes ephemeral containers, a temporary container type that can be run inside a Pod for diagnostic purposes. They are intended for troubleshooting and should not be used for running primary application workloads.

etcd.md.title: etcd Overview
etcd.md.summary: This document introduces etcd, a consistent and highly-available key-value store. It explains that etcd serves as the backing store for all cluster data in Kubernetes.

event.md.title: Kubernetes Event Object
event.md.summary: This document describes the Kubernetes Event object, which records state changes or notable occurrences within the cluster. It advises consumers to treat events as informative, best-effort data due to their limited retention and evolving nature.

eviction.md.title: Pod Eviction Process
eviction.md.summary: This document explains the concept of eviction, which is the process of terminating one or more Pods running on Nodes. It distinguishes between two types: Node-pressure eviction and API-initiated eviction.

extend-kubernetes.md.title: Extending Kubernetes Cluster Functionality
extend-kubernetes.md.summary: This guide details how to customize a Kubernetes cluster beyond simple configuration changes. It focuses on software extensions, covering various patterns and points for deep integration.

extensions.md.title: Kubernetes Extensions Overview
extensions.md.summary: This document introduces Kubernetes Extensions, which are software components designed to deeply integrate with Kubernetes to support new types of hardware. It notes that many pre-installed extensions are available in hosted Kubernetes distributions.

feature-gates.md.title: Kubernetes Feature Gates
feature-gates.md.summary: This document explains feature gates, which are opaque string keys used to control the enablement of specific Kubernetes features within a cluster. They can be toggled on or off using the --feature-gates command-line flag on Kubernetes components.

finalizer.md.title: Kubernetes Finalizers Explained
finalizer.md.summary: This document explains Kubernetes Finalizers, which are namespaced keys that instruct Kubernetes to delay the full deletion of resources. They alert controllers to perform necessary cleanup actions before the object is permanently removed.

flexvolume.md.title: FlexVolume Interface for Volume Plugins
flexvolume.md.summary: This document describes FlexVolume, a deprecated interface used for creating out-of-tree volume plugins in Kubernetes. It explains that the Container Storage Interface (CSI) is the newer standard addressing FlexVolume's limitations.

gateway.md.title: Gateway API Reference and Design
gateway.md.summary: This document describes the Gateway API, an extensible, role-oriented mechanism for configuring network services. It details the resource model, including GatewayClass, Gateway, HTTPRoute, and GRPCRoute, and outlines design principles like role-orientation and expressiveness.

glossary-api-eviction.md.title: API-initiated Pod Eviction
glossary-api-eviction.md.summary: This document explains API-initiated eviction, the process of triggering graceful pod termination by creating an Eviction object via the Eviction API. It details how this mechanism respects PodDisruptionBudgets and terminationGracePeriodSeconds.

glossary-configmap.md.title: ConfigMap Overview
glossary-configmap.md.summary: ConfigMaps are API objects used to store non-confidential data in key-value pairs. They allow applications to consume configuration as environment variables, command-line arguments, or volume files, decoupling configuration from container images.

glossary-container-lifecycle-hooks.md.title: Container Lifecycle Hooks
glossary-container-lifecycle-hooks.md.summary: This document explains container lifecycle hooks, which allow users to execute custom code when specific events occur during a container's lifecycle. It details the PostStart and PreStop hooks available for containers.

glossary-controller.md.title: Kubernetes Controller Overview
glossary-controller.md.summary: This document explains that Kubernetes controllers are control loops that monitor the cluster's state and work to move it toward a desired state. They interact with the apiserver and include core components like the deployment and daemonset controllers.

glossary-cri.md.title: Kubernetes Container Runtime Interface (CRI)
glossary-cri.md.summary: This document describes the Container Runtime Interface (CRI), which is the primary gRPC protocol. It defines how the kubelet communicates with the container runtime on Kubernetes nodes.

glossary-deployment.md.title: Deployment Object Overview
glossary-deployment.md.summary: This document describes the API object used to manage replicated applications, typically by running stateless Pods across a cluster. It notes that StatefulSets should be used for workloads requiring local state.

glossary-downward-api.md.title: Kubernetes Downward API
glossary-downward-api.md.summary: This document explains the Kubernetes Downward API, a mechanism that exposes Pod and container field values to code running inside a container. It allows applications to access self-information without directly interacting with the Kubernetes API.

glossary-dra.md.title: Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) in Kubernetes
glossary-dra.md.summary: This document explains Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA), a Kubernetes feature for requesting and sharing resources among Pods. It details how device drivers and admins define device classes for workloads to claim and how Kubernetes allocates matching devices.

glossary-garbage-collection.md.title: Kubernetes Garbage Collection Mechanisms
glossary-garbage-collection.md.summary: This document explains garbage collection, which is the collective term for mechanisms Kubernetes uses to clean up cluster resources. It details how Kubernetes handles the cleanup of various resources like unused containers, failed Pods, and completed Jobs.

glossary-kube-scheduler.md.title: kube-scheduler Overview
glossary-kube-scheduler.md.summary: This document describes the kube-scheduler, a control plane component responsible for selecting appropriate nodes for newly created Pods. It details the various factors considered during the scheduling decision process.

glossary-kubectl.md.title: Kubectl Command Line Tool
glossary-kubectl.md.summary: This document describes Kubectl, the command-line tool used to interact with a Kubernetes cluster's control plane. It explains how to use kubectl to create, inspect, update, and delete Kubernetes objects via the Kubernetes API.

glossary-kubernetes-api.md.title: Kubernetes API Overview
glossary-kubernetes-api.md.summary: This document describes the Kubernetes API, which is the HTTP interface enabling communication and state manipulation of Kubernetes objects. It explains how resources are managed declaratively through RESTful calls.

glossary-logging.md.title: Cluster and Application Logging
glossary-logging.md.summary: This document explains that logs are records of events generated by a cluster or application. They are essential tools for debugging issues and monitoring the overall activity within the cluster.

glossary-mixed-version-proxy.md.title: Mixed Version Proxy (MVP) for kube-apiserver
glossary-mixed-version-proxy.md.summary: This feature allows the kube-apiserver to proxy resource requests to a different peer API server. It is used in clusters with multiple API servers running different Kubernetes versions to ensure requests are served correctly.

glossary-node-pressure-eviction.md.title: Node-Pressure Eviction Explained
glossary-node-pressure-eviction.md.summary: This document describes node-pressure eviction, a kubelet process that proactively terminates pods. It explains how the kubelet monitors resource usage (CPU, memory, disk) and evicts pods to prevent resource starvation.

glossary-pod-lifecycle.md.title: Pod Lifecycle States
glossary-pod-lifecycle.md.summary: This document describes the Pod Lifecycle, which outlines the sequence of states a Pod goes through during its existence. It details the five possible Pod phases: Pending, Running, Succeeded, Failed, and Unknown.

glossary-pod-security-policy.md.title: Pod Security Policy (Deprecated)
glossary-pod-security-policy.md.summary: This document describes Pod Security Policy, a former Kubernetes API used to enforce security restrictions on pod creation and updates. It notes that this policy has been deprecated since Kubernetes v1.21 and removed in v1.25.

glossary-secret.md.title: Managing Secrets in Kubernetes
glossary-secret.md.summary: This document explains the purpose and handling of Secrets, which store sensitive data like passwords and tokens. It details how Secrets can be referenced by Pods and contrasts them with ConfigMaps.

glossary-security-context.md.title: Pod/Container Security Context Configuration
glossary-security-context.md.summary: This document explains the `securityContext` field, which defines privilege and access control settings for a Pod or container. It details how to configure user, group, and security policies like SELinux or AppArmor.
